title: Learner 01 | Day 156: Rate limits, quotas, and fairness
body:
## Goal

Rate limits, quotas, and fairness

## Implementation contract

**File:** `src/learnforge/specializations/learner_01/core/admission.py`

**Method/unit:** `admit_prediction`

**Why here:** This is inside your owned AI/ML capability and the named layer. Model/data SDK details stay in adapters, rules in core, and commands/results in experience. It plugs into the same shared project architecture as other capabilities.

**Inputs and expected outputs:** First request consumes one token; repeated bursts are bounded; one tenant cannot starve all others.

**Boundaries:** Keep the change inside the owned capability and preserve accepted behavior.

## Research hints

1. Research **Rate limits, quotas, and fairness**. Which rule explains your named unit’s behavior?
2. Search `site:sre.google Rate limits quotas and fairness`; use [Google SRE book](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/) for the relevant small section.
3. Predict one changed input/timing case, run it, and explain each changed value before applying the finding.

## Done

- [ ] Demonstrate this unit’s normal and boundary/failure cases in the working feature.
- [ ] Show the actual run and explain one changed case using concrete values.

**Question of the Day:** What must a parent coordinator track across parallel branches?

**Review with @YogeshPatil991:** run the named unit; show actual output and each relevant line’s purpose, before/after values and project contribution.
